questions.q: What does an LLM actually add to the root cause analysis process taught in Fabric & Real-Time Analytics Lesson 58?
options: Speed on the first step — reading a wall of logs and proposing a starting hypothesis
A replacement for reproducing and isolating the failure
A guaranteed, verified root cause with no further checking needed
The ability to fix the pipeline automatically without human review
questions.explain: RCA still means reproduce, isolate, and confirm — an LLM just accelerates the initial read of logs and error context.

questions.q: What context does a pipeline failure's RCA draft actually need to be useful?
options: A list of every engineer who has ever touched the pipeline
Only the error message, with nothing else
The exact error and stack trace, the log lines before the failure, the failed stage, and anything that changed recently
The entire codebase of the pipeline
questions.explain: Without that context, the draft is just a guess dressed up as a confident answer.

questions.q: Why isn't an LLM's confident, well-organized RCA draft treated as a verdict?
options: Because confidence in a draft always means it's correct
Because the model is pattern-matching the error against similar failures it has seen before, with no access to your actual system or recent history
Because RCA drafts are always factually wrong
Because LLMs are incapable of producing organized text
questions.explain: The model has no access to your data's real history or a deploy that isn't reflected in the pasted logs, so every claim still needs confirming.

questions.q: On what kind of failure does an AI-drafted RCA earn its keep the most, per this lesson?
options: A completely novel failure nobody has seen before
High-volume, repetitive failures where it can confirm or rule out a human's existing instinct in seconds
Failures that occurred before the pipeline was built
Failures with no logs available at all
questions.explain: Repetitive failures have patterns the LLM can match against; genuinely novel failures have none, which is exactly Lesson 61's honest-limits point.

questions.q: What should happen to an LLM's RCA draft before it goes into an incident report?
options: It should replace the need for logs in future incidents
It should be pasted in verbatim without review
Every claim in it should be actually checked and confirmed, the same way any human hypothesis would be
It should be discarded entirely and never used
questions.explain: The draft is the first thing to check, not the conclusion — confirmation is still mandatory.
